Petra: Nabataean, Greek and Roman crossroads
Gandhara: Greek, Buddhist and Indian exchange
Dunhuang: Buddhist, Manichaean and Nestorian exchange
Kilwa: Bantu, Arab and Persian blend
Kyiv: Norse, Slavic and Byzantine blend
Manila: Chinese, Spanish and Mexican exchange
Spice wars: Banda and the Moluccas
Euphrates frontier with Parthia and Persia

entities.nt: Southern Mesopotamian colonies and trading posts planted far up the rivers and across the highlands, the first long-distance urban network.
entities.hubs: Uruk, Habuba Kabira, Godin Tepe, Susa

entities.nt: Carnelian, lapis, copper and timber carried by sea between the Indus cities, Oman, Bahrain (Dilmun) and Ur.
entities.hubs: Mohenjo-daro, Ur, Lothal, Dilmun (Bahrain), Magan (Oman)

entities.nt: Tyrian and later Carthaginian ports strung across the Mediterranean to the Atlantic coast of Iberia and Morocco.
entities.hubs: Tyre, Carthage, Gadir (Cádiz), Kition, Motya, Nora, Ibiza, Mogador

entities.nt: Hundreds of Greek city-founded colonies and trading ports around the Mediterranean and the Black Sea.
entities.hubs: Athens, Syracuse, Massalia, Miletus, Byzantion, Sinope, Olbia, Panticapaeum, Neapolis, Emporion

entities.nt: Frankincense and myrrh carried by camel caravan from southern Arabia along the Hejaz to Gaza and the Mediterranean.
entities.hubs: Marib, Petra, Sumhuram, Shabwa, Najran, Mecca, Dedan (AlUla), Gaza

entities.nt: The Achaemenid imperial post road with way stations and relay riders from Sardis to Susa.
entities.hubs: Sardis, Susa, Gordion, Samosata, Nineveh

entities.nt: The overland web of caravan routes joining China, Central Asia, Persia and the Mediterranean.
entities.hubs: Chang'an, Kashgar, Samarkand, Merv, Baghdad, Constantinople, Dunhuang, Turpan, Khotan, Bukhara, Balkh, Rayy, Palmyra, Antioch

entities.nt: Monsoon-driven sea routes joining China, Southeast Asia, India, the Gulf, the Red Sea and East Africa.
entities.hubs: Guangzhou, Malacca, Calicut, Aden, Quanzhou, Colombo, Muscat, Hormuz, Basra, Jeddah, Mogadishu, Mombasa, Kilwa

entities.nt: Annual pilgrim caravans from Damascus, Cairo, Baghdad and Yemen converging on Mecca, with organised water stops and escorts.
entities.hubs: Damascus, Cairo, Medina, Mecca, Kufa, Sana'a

entities.nt: Camel caravans carrying gold, salt, cloth and people between the Maghreb, Egypt and the Sahel.
entities.hubs: Timbuktu, Kano, Sijilmasa, Taghaza, Gao, Djenné, Tripoli, Ghadames, Agadez, Cairo, Njimi (Kanem)

entities.nt: Stone-built port towns trading gold from the Zimbabwe plateau, ivory and slaves for Indian Ocean cloth, beads and ceramics.
entities.hubs: Mombasa, Kilwa, Great Zimbabwe, Mogadishu, Lamu, Zanzibar, Sofala

entities.w: Trade route from the Varangians to the Greeks
entities.nt: Rus' and Scandinavian traders carried furs, slaves and silver along the rivers to Constantinople and, by the Volga, to Baghdad.
entities.hubs: Novgorod, Kyiv, Constantinople, Birka, Staraya Ladoga, Smolensk, Bolghar, Itil, Baghdad

entities.nt: A league of north German and Baltic trading towns with walled trading posts (kontore) from London to Novgorod.
entities.hubs: Lübeck, Bruges, London (Steelyard), Bergen, Novgorod, Hamburg, Cologne, Danzig, Riga, Visby, Reval (Tallinn), Königsberg

entities.nt: Venice's string of fortified ports, galley convoys and trading quarters from the Adriatic to the Black Sea and the Levant.
entities.hubs: Venice, Candia, Constantinople, Zara, Corfu, Modon, Famagusta, Acre, Alexandria, Tana

entities.nt: Genoese colonies and banking houses from the western Mediterranean to Caffa on the Black Sea.
entities.hubs: Genoa, Pera (Galata), Caffa, Tunis, Chios, Seville

entities.nt: A continental relay of post stations with horses, riders and passports linking the Mongol khanates.
entities.hubs: Khanbaliq (Beijing), Karakorum, Sarai, Tabriz, Almaliq, Otrar, Urgench, Moscow

entities.nt: Some 40,000 km of imperial roads with relay runners (chasqui), storehouses and way stations linking Cusco to the four quarters.
entities.hubs: Cusco, Quito, Cajamarca, Lake Titicaca, Potosí, Santiago

entities.nt: The Portuguese state's annual armada route round Africa, with fortified ports (feitorias) from Mozambique to Macau and Japan.
entities.hubs: Lisbon, Goa, Malacca, Macau, Mozambique Island, Cochin, Nagasaki, Hormuz

entities.nt: Convoyed fleets carrying silver and goods between Seville and the Spanish Indies through a few licensed ports.
entities.hubs: Seville, Havana, Cartagena de Indias, Portobelo, Veracruz

entities.nt: Annual galleons carrying Chinese silk and porcelain and Mexican silver across the Pacific between Manila and Acapulco.
entities.hubs: Manila, Acapulco

entities.nt: The Dutch chartered company's fleet, forts and factories from the Cape to Batavia, Ceylon and Dejima.
entities.hubs: Amsterdam, Cape Town, Batavia, Dejima (Nagasaki), Colombo, Ambon

entities.nt: Company posts, canoe brigades and river portages carrying furs from the Canadian interior to Hudson Bay and Montreal.
entities.hubs: York Factory, Montreal, Norway House, Fort Edmonton, Fort Vancouver, Fort William, Red River (Winnipeg)

entities.nt: The forced shipment of some 12 million Africans to the Americas along fixed commercial routes, run by European merchant houses, chartered companies and African coastal and inland suppliers.
entities.hubs: Elmina, Luanda, Salvador, Liverpool, Gorée, Rio de Janeiro, Bridgetown, Kingston, Charleston, Havana

entities.nt: A Moscow-directed network of national communist parties, couriers and front organisations.
entities.hubs: Moscow, Berlin, Paris, Shanghai, Mexico City, Madrid, London

entities.n: Chinese Communist base areas and Long March
entities.nt: Rural base areas held by the Red Army and party, and the 1934-35 retreat between them.
entities.hubs: Ruijin (Jiangxi Soviet), Yan'an, Zunyi, Luding Bridge

entities.nt: Stone-paved military roads with mansiones, milestones and the imperial courier service (cursus publicus) tying the empire to Rome.
entities.hubs: Rome, Byzantium, Lugdunum (Lyon), Antioch, Brundisium, Dyrrachium, Thessalonica, Mediolanum (Milan), Colonia Agrippina, Tarraco, Gades, Aelia Capitolina, Alexandria, Carnuntum

entities.nt: A Red Sea and Nile highland state whose port of Adulis tied the Horn of Africa to Rome, Arabia and India.
entities.hubs: Aksum, Adulis, Berenike, Meroë, Muziris/Barygaza (India)

entities.nt: Letter-linked congregations along Roman roads and sea lanes from Jerusalem to Rome, Alexandria and Carthage.
entities.hubs: Jerusalem, Antioch, Rome, Alexandria, Ephesus, Corinth, Thessalonica, Carthage

entities.nt: Monasteries, pilgrims and translators carrying Buddhism from the Ganges plain along the Silk Road and sea lanes to China, Korea, Japan and Southeast Asia.
entities.hubs: Pataliputra, Chang'an, Bodh Gaya, Taxila, Bamiyan, Dunhuang, Luoyang, Gyeongju, Nara, Anuradhapura, Palembang

entities.nt: A Syriac Christian network of dioceses and monasteries from Mesopotamia across Central Asia to China and the Malabar coast.
entities.hubs: Seleucia-Ctesiphon, Chang'an, Merv, Samarkand, Kashgar, Kochi (Malabar)

entities.grp: Latin Christendom and the Catholic world
entities.nt: A centrally governed order with colleges and missions from Rome to Goa, Macau, Beijing, Quebec and the Paraguayan reductions.
entities.hubs: Rome, Goa, Beijing, Macau, Quebec, Asunción, Salvador

entities.nt: A Malay sea power controlling the Strait of Malacca through port polities that tolled and protected shipping between China and India.
entities.hubs: Palembang, Jambi, Kedah, Nakhon Si Thammarat, Java ports

entities.nt: An artificial waterway system carrying grain tribute from the Yangtze delta to the northern capitals.
entities.hubs: Hangzhou, Beijing, Suzhou, Yangzhou, Huai'an, Jining, Tianjin

entities.nt: Caravan tracks carrying tea from Yunnan and Sichuan to Tibet in exchange for horses.
entities.hubs: Lhasa, Pu'er, Dali, Lijiang, Ya'an, Kangding

entities.nt: Clan, dialect and guild associations linking Fujian and Guangdong to the ports of Southeast Asia and beyond.
entities.hubs: Xiamen, Singapore, Manila, Batavia, Bangkok

entities.nt: A chartered company that grew from factories into a territorial state with its own army, fleet and monopoly trade.
entities.hubs: London, Bombay, Calcutta, Canton, Cape Town, Madras, Singapore

entities.nt: Bengal opium auctioned at Calcutta, carried by country traders to Lintin and Canton and paid for in silver and tea.
entities.hubs: Calcutta, Lintin Island, Patna, Bombay

entities.nt: The rail spine of the Russian east, 9,000 km from Moscow to the Pacific, with later branches to Mongolia and China.
entities.hubs: Moscow, Vladivostok, Yekaterinburg, Novosibirsk, Irkutsk, Chita

entities.nt: The standardised box and a few dozen hub ports now carry most manufactured trade between East Asia, Europe and North America.
entities.hubs: Shanghai, Singapore, Rotterdam, Los Angeles–Long Beach, Jebel Ali, Suez, New York–New Jersey

entities.nt: Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan collected tribute from some 38 provinces while pochteca merchants carried goods and intelligence beyond the frontier.
entities.hubs: Tenochtitlan, Texcoco, Tlacopan, Oaxaca, Tochtepec, Xoconochco

entities.nt: Five (later six) nations bound by the Great Law and a shared council fire at Onondaga, acting as one in diplomacy, war and the fur trade.
entities.hubs: Onondaga (council fire), Mohawk, Oneida, Cayuga, Seneca

entities.nt: Navigators who crossed the open Pacific by canoe, settling and keeping exchange between islands from Samoa and Tonga to Hawaiʻi, Rapa Nui and Aotearoa.
entities.hubs: Samoa, Tahiti (Society Islands), Hawaiʻi, Aotearoa, Fiji, Marquesas, Rapa Nui, Rarotonga

entities.nt: Laid by British and other cable companies, the first global electric communications network, joining empires, markets and newspapers.
entities.hubs: Valentia (Ireland), Bombay, Singapore, Heart's Content, Alexandria, Aden, Hong Kong, Darwin, Sydney

entities.n: International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement
entities.w: International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement
entities.nt: A federation of national societies and the neutral ICRC in Geneva, carrying relief and protection into war and disaster zones.
entities.hubs: Geneva (ICRC), Istanbul, Nairobi, New Delhi, Washington, Sydney

entities.nt: A treaty organisation of member states with headquarters, agencies, peacekeeping and humanitarian operations across the world.
entities.hubs: New York (HQ), Geneva, Nairobi, Vienna, Addis Ababa, Bangkok

entities.grp: Latin Christendom and the Catholic world
entities.nt: The western Church: dioceses, monasteries, tithes, canon law, universities and the Latin language held Western Europe together across its kingdoms, directed from Rome.
entities.hubs: Rome, Avignon, Cluny, Paris, Canterbury, Cologne, Santiago de Compostela, Kraków

entities.grp: Latin Christendom and the Catholic world
entities.nt: A global hierarchy of dioceses, parishes, orders, schools and hospitals, with the Holy See at Rome and the Jesuit and mendicant missions carrying it across the world.
entities.hubs: Rome (Holy See), Mexico City, São Paulo, Kinshasa, Manila

entities.nt: A communion of self-governing churches, with patriarchates at Constantinople, Antioch, Alexandria, Jerusalem and Moscow, tying together the Balkans, Rus', Georgia and Ethiopia.
entities.hubs: Constantinople, Moscow, Kyiv, Mount Athos, Belgrade

entities.nt: Successive horse-nomad federations held the grasslands from Manchuria to the Danube: the Xiongnu, Göktürks, Khazars, Mongols and the Golden Horde, living off herds, tribute and taxing the caravans.
entities.hubs: Karakorum, Sarai, Ötükän, Itil

entities.nt: Ming and Qing diplomacy made the Chinese court the centre of an order of tributary kingdoms, whose missions carried trade and recognition under imperial supervision.
entities.hubs: Beijing, Hanseong (Seoul), Thăng Long (Hanoi), Shuri (Ryukyu), Ayutthaya

entities.nt: A chartered fur-trading company that governed Alaska and posts down the Pacific coast to California, supplied by sea from Siberia.
entities.hubs: Novo-Arkhangelsk (Sitka), Petropavlovsk, Kodiak, Fort Ross

entities.nt: A collective-defence alliance with an integrated command, shared standards, bases and pre-positioned logistics across North America and Europe.
entities.hubs: Brussels (HQ), Washington, Ramstein, Norfolk

entities.nt: The Soviet-led military alliance and its economic council, with Soviet garrisons, shared railways and gas and oil pipelines binding Eastern Europe to Moscow.
entities.hubs: Moscow, Warsaw, Berlin, Budapest

entities.nt: A union of states with a single market, shared law, common borders and trans-European transport, energy and payment networks.
entities.hubs: Brussels, Strasbourg, Luxembourg, Frankfurt (ECB)

entities.nt: A family that held its lands by marriage as much as by war: Austria, Bohemia, Hungary, Spain with its Italian and Burgundian possessions, joined by kin, credit and the Spanish Road, the military supply corridor from Milan to Brussels.
entities.hubs: Vienna, Madrid, Brussels, Prague, Innsbruck, Milan, Naples, Barcelona, Seville, Budapest

entities.nt: A family bank with branches in the great trading cities, moving papal revenue and merchant credit by bills of exchange across Latin Europe.
entities.hubs: Florence, Rome, Bruges, Venice, Milan, Geneva, Lyon, Avignon, London

entities.grp: Latin Christendom and the Catholic world
entities.nt: A military order that was also an international bank and landowner: commanderies across Europe fed money, men and horses to the Holy Land and held deposits for kings and pilgrims.
entities.hubs: Jerusalem, Acre, Paris (the Temple), Limassol, London (the Temple), Marseille, Tomar
